text:
maria: heads up — p99 latency on g5x-1 inference pool jumped ~2.3x starting 03:12 UTC. throughput fell ~50%. noticed by latency alerts.

derek: seeing it on our dashboards too. p50 steady, p95 up a bit, p99 really moved. any recent deploys?

sasha: no model deploys from infra side. infra-bot: kernel-selector version 1.9.4 rolled at 00:30 UTC, but no fleet-wide change after that. driver versions: some hosts reported auto-up of nvidia-driver 545.44 -> 545.67 around 02:50 UTC (from fleet telemetry).

maria: good catch. attaching quick sampling from runtime logs (trimmed):
```
[03:11:57] selected_kernel=flash_attn_fwd_fp16_v2 workspace=12.3MB latency=3.6ms
[03:12:03] selected_kernel=triton_flash_noalloc_fp16 workspace=8.1MB latency=8.9ms
[03:12:04] selected_kernel=gemm_fallback_fp16 workspace=0.9MB latency=14.2ms
[03:12:10] selected_kernel=triton_flash_noalloc_fp16 workspace=8.1MB latency=11.8ms
```
maria: looks like kernel selection started flipping away from flash_attn_v2 to triton/gemm fallback for identical requests.

ted: pv: ran a micro repro against a single machine with the exact driver version change. script: `python perf_probe.py --model llama-7b --seq 64 --batch 8 --iters 200`

ted: repro results: on 545.44 p99 ~185ms, on 545.67 p99 ~420ms. raw selector traces show workspace query returns different free-memory/workspace hint which makes our kernel_fingerprint hash change.

sasha: kv cache metrics show a coincident drop in kv_hit_rate: 0.97 -> 0.62 around the same time; evictions spiked. suspect bigger workspace or different kernel layout causing more memory pressure and KV thrash.

maria: interesting. so hypothesis chain: driver patch changed cudaMalloc behavior or workspace-query behavior -> causes kernel selector fingerprint mismatch -> selects alternate kernels (triton/gemm) with different memory patterns -> workspace pressure -> KV evictions -> tail latency increase and throughput drop.

derek: can we confirm by forcing kernel preference? try `KERNEL_SELECTOR_PREFER=flash_attn_v2` env override on a canary host.

ted: applied override to 1 host in pool (canary-23). results: p99 fell back to ~190ms, kv_hit_rate recovered to 0.95. logs show selected_kernel pinned to flash_attn_fwd_fp16_v2 consistently.

maria: good mitigation. rolling that override to 10% of the pool now while we triage fleet-wide. posting a small rollback plan:
- step 1: pin kernel selector pref to flash_attn_v2 (env) for affected fleets (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
- step 2: pin driver to 545.44 on most affected hosts via fleet manager (requires rolling reboot)
- step 3: collect extended telemetry and heap/freemem traces for fingerprint fix

sasha: also capturing `nvml` memory profiles and `cudaMemGetInfo` traces during requests to confirm workspace footprint delta. attaching sample NVML snippet:
```
GPU 0: mem_total=32768MB mem_used_before=6400MB cudaMemGetInfo_free=26368MB
after kernel alloc: cudaMemGetInfo_free=25040MB (delta ~1328MB)
```
sasha: on the newer driver the delta reported is larger for the same kernel which explains eviction.

oncall-bot: incident created INC-2026-2001 (severity: high). paging oncall.

maria: immediate next steps: keep kernel preference override on for now; infra to triage driver rollbacks; runtime team to add a short-circuit: if selector chooses non-flash kernel for N identical requests in T seconds, prefer previous kernel unless workspace > threshold.

derek: working on a patch to make kernel_fingerprint incorporate a stable heuristic (model+seq+batch+arch) and ignore noisy workspace hints unless they differ by > 25%. will push PR and run integration tests.

ted: long term we should: (1) make selector able to surface a confidence metric and waterfall to previous kernel, (2) add a KV eviction backpressure signal to selector, (3) add driver-version aware tests in our CI.

maria: timeline/owner summary:
- mitigation (done): kernel pref override -> maria/ted
- rollback driver (in progress): infra (sasha)
- selector robustness patch (in review): eng-runtime (derek)
- permanent deploy + obsv changes: eng-sre/eng-runtime (maria/derek)

sasha: infra discovered ~120 hosts with auto-updated driver; scheduling rollbacks in waves. will keep this thread updated.

replay-bot: replay job 2001234567-1 queued (same request shape) to validate after rollback.

maria: re-check: did any customer-facing APIs degrade? support, please advise.

sasha: support says a small percentage of requests got transient 502s from timeouts but no broad user-facing outages. emailing affected customers for transparency.

maria: thanks. will follow up with a post-incident doc after root- cause patch and driver hotfix. closing loop: keep this thread for updates only.
